title: Dhanush Breaks Silence on National Award Backlash: 'There Were Better Films Than Raayan'
excerpt: The actor-director acknowledged criticism of his Best Tamil Film win while listing a career's worth of overlooked performances.
body:
• Dhanush publicly acknowledged that 'there were definitely better films' than his directorial effort Raayan, which won Best Tamil Film at the 72nd National Film Awards
  • He also received a Special Mention for Best Actor for his performance in Captain Miller, calling it his 'finest performance to date'
  • The awards brought Dhanush's National Award count to three — two for acting (Aadukalam, Asuran) and his first as a director
  • He urged critics to celebrate his career achievements rather than focus solely on the Raayan controversy

Dhanush has waded into the controversy surrounding his 72nd National Film Awards wins with a rare act of public candour — acknowledging at a fan event on Sunday that his directorial work Raayan was not the best Tamil film of 2024, even as he defended his body of work and asked critics to look at the bigger picture.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=lGnnWVcD1yE

A Disarming Admission

""Some things simply fall into place on their own, no matter how hard you try; that is exactly how it happened for me," he said."

"For Raayan, I got a National Film Award. That year, there were definitely better films than that one," Dhanush told the audience, drawing a mix of surprise and applause. "The fans of those films expressed their love, and I fully respect them." He did not name specific titles, but the comments are widely understood as a nod to films like Maharaja and Amaran, which many in the Tamil film industry felt were stronger contenders.

https://x.com/iammoviebuff007/status/2081362805412782086

Raayan, Dhanush's second directorial venture and his 50th film as an actor, is a revenge drama that received mixed reviews upon release. The Hindu described it as an attempt to "turn an ordinary story into something more with well-written setting and measured storytelling" that "falls disappointingly short." India Today gave it 2.5 out of 5 stars, noting it "lacks emotional depth."

A Career of Near-Misses

Having made the admission, Dhanush pivoted to the broader arc of his career. He listed film after film — Adhu Oru Kana Kaalam, Pudhupettai, 3, Mayakkam Enna, Vada Chennai, Karnan, Maryan, Raanjhanaa — each name met with cheers from the crowd. His point was clear: for every award he has won, there were years when recognition eluded performances that deserved it.

"Some things simply fall into place on their own, no matter how hard you try; that is exactly how it happened for me," he said.

Captain Miller: The Quieter Win

Less controversial but arguably more personally significant was Dhanush's Special Mention for Best Actor for Captain Miller, Arun Matheswaran's period revenge drama about a village leader fighting British colonial rule. "This recognition for Captain Miller is especially close to me because I have always believed it to be my finest performance to date," Dhanush wrote on social media after the awards were announced.

Director Matheswaran was equally moved. "Seeing Dhanush sir getting recognised for this film is a testament to the efforts he took," he told Cinema Express, adding that the film also won the National Award for Best Feature Film Promoting National, Social and Environmental Values.

With three National Awards — two for acting (Aadukalam in 2010 and Asuran in 2019) and now his first as a director — Dhanush has built a record that few of his contemporaries in Tamil cinema can match. Whether Raayan deserved the specific honour it received will remain a matter of debate. What is harder to argue is that the artist behind it has earned his place.
